name: Design four bass types from scratch with fit-to-kick rules: a punchy 808 (sine, hold and 1.5 s decay, a 35 ms pitch-envelope punch, tube drive, low boost, attack delayed 80-100 ms when the kick already punches), a pluck bass (mono square through an enveloped 24 dB low-pass plus a wide unison top layer), a sidechained saw growl, and a click-free sine sub
goal: Four punchy bass recipes. 808: one sine osc, attack near 0 (raise slightly until the click disappears), hold about 300-400 ms, decay about 1.5 s, sustain 0; a little wavetable bend/warp for character; a second envelope (attack about 0.5 ms, hold 0, decay about 35 ms, sustain 0, release about 15 ms) routed to master tune for a kick-like pitch punch (set amount to the middle); tube distortion with mix pulled back; EQ lift around 100 Hz. If the kick already supplies the punch, raise the 808 attack to about 80-100 ms so it fills in behind the kick instead of sidechaining. Pluck/house bass: mono voice, square wave through a 24 dB low-pass, short attack, no hold, low sustain, some release; the same envelope also drives cutoff for the pluck; drive the filter a little; add a second osc (PWM-type wave, 5-7 unison voices, detuned) for a wide top, keep content below about 100-150 Hz mono, reverb and delay with low cut. Growl bass: saw with a low-pass, second osc with 7-8 unison voices, mono, very short release, an LFO shaped as a sidechain duck on both osc levels, cutoff on a macro, then boost about 140 Hz to keep it a bass. Sub: sine, one voice, mono/legato, attack about 5 ms and a short release to avoid clicks.

source.title: Bass Sound Design: 808s, Plucks, Growls and Sub Bass
source.transcript_note: Auto-generated YouTube Show transcript; values are as spoken and approximate where the speaker says 'about' or 'around'.

prerequisites: A synth with envelopes, mod matrix (envelope → pitch), unison, mono mode, LFO shapes
A drum loop with a kick for context

inputs.name: kick
inputs.description: The kick it must sit with

outputs.name: bass_patch
outputs.description: Bass patch of the chosen type

outputs.name: fit_notes
outputs.description: How the bass was fitted around the kick (attack delay, LFO duck or sidechain)

constraints: Original synthesis recipe; not affiliated with any vendor named in the source. Recreate in browser/Web Audio (Polyrhythm Studio) or any hybrid synth with comparable modules; no presets, banks or samples copied.
Vendor wavetable names (e.g. a named PWM wave) are replaced by generic shapes.
Keep below about 100-150 Hz mono; put width only on higher layers.
Reverb on bass: cut its lows (ideally on a separate return).
For Matt's cinematic/ambient tracks the 808 and sub recipes and the attack-delay trick are the most relevant; the growl is optional for driving sections.
Auto-generated YouTube Show transcript; values are as spoken and approximate where the speaker says 'about' or 'around'.

steps.action: 808 body: sine osc, attack near 0 then raised just enough to remove the click, hold about 300-400 ms, decay about 1.5 s, sustain 0; add a slight bend/warp to the wave for character.
steps.expect: A clean sub tone that holds then decays.

steps.action: 808 punch: second envelope (attack about 0.5 ms, hold 0, decay about 35 ms, sustain 0, release about 15 ms) → master/global tune; set the amount between too little and too much.
steps.expect: A kick-like pitch blip at the start of each note.

steps.action: 808 FX: tube distortion with mix pulled back, EQ lift around 100 Hz. Play with the drums: if both kick and 808 punch, raise the 808 attack to about 80-100 ms so the kick provides the transient.
steps.expect: The 808 fills behind the kick without clashing.

steps.action: Pluck bass: mono voicing, square osc into a 24 dB low-pass; amp envelope with tiny attack, no hold, low sustain, a bit of release; route the same envelope to cutoff and add a little filter drive.

Pluck top layer: second osc with a PWM-style wave, 5-7 unison voices, detune set for width, through the same filter at lower level; add reverb and delay with their lows cut; keep lows mono below about 100-150 Hz.
steps.expect: Wide upper texture over a solid mono low end.

steps.action: Growl bass: saw + low-pass, second saw osc with 7-8 unison voices, mono, very short release; draw an LFO shaped like a sidechain duck and route it to both osc levels; put cutoff (and optionally reverb/delay mix) on macros; boost around 140 Hz.
steps.expect: A rhythmic ducking growl that sits around the kick.

steps.action: Sub: sine, 1 voice, mono/legato, attack about 5 ms, short-but-not-instant release; play low.
steps.expect: Smooth sub with no clicks at note start/end; overlapping notes glide.

verification: 808 shows a pitch drop over the first ~35 ms and decays over about 1.5 s.
With the kick, the 808 (with delayed attack) does not double the transient.
Low end below about 120 Hz is mono for all four types.
Sub notes start and stop without audible clicks.
